info.title: Lumeus Assets API
info.description:
Lumeus Assets API on Stellar. Sign up at https://app.lumeus.dev: Free, Starter, Growth and Scale plans are self-serve, Enterprise by agreement.

- **Pricing.** Testnet is free: Testnet requests cost no credits and are never billed. Each organization can make 10,000 Testnet requests a day across Activity, Assets and RPC (unlimited on Enterprise); the count resets at 00:00 UTC, and a request over it answers 429 rate_limited with Retry-After set to the seconds until then. Mainnet requests draw from the plan's monthly credits. Plans, limits and credit weights: `GET https://api.lumeus.dev/v1/plans`.
- **Authentication.** Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, the same keys as Activity and RPC. Testnet: `lum_test_…`; Mainnet: `lum_live_…`. A key works only on its own network, so pick the server that matches it (the other network answers 401). Publishable `lum_pub_…` keys work only on the routes marked "Publishable keys allowed", from an allowed browser origin.
- **Headers.** Every response except `GET /readyz` carries X-Request-Id; authenticated responses carry RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset; 429 and 503 carry Retry-After.
- **Errors.** JSON with a machine-readable code (see [errors](/guides/errors)). A path with an empty, `.` or `..` segment answers 400 invalid_request, a trailing slash answers 404 not_found, and a method the path does not accept answers 405 with an Allow header.
- **CORS.** Browser calls (CORS) are allowed from https://docs.lumeus.dev (the Try it playground of this reference) and https://app.lumeus.dev only, without cookies; responses expose ETag, Link, Location, Retry-After, X-Request-Id, X-Lumeus-Operation-Id, X-Lumeus-Idempotency and RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset (errors included). Other websites cannot read responses made with a server key: use a publishable key with your own allowed origins ([browser keys](/guides/browser-keys)).

get.description:
Every balance the address holds: XLM, trustlines (including zero balances with include=zero), liquidity pool shares, and SAC and custom-token balances held in contract storage, live or archived. Sorted by asset. Each record says how it was determined (source, verified); the completeness block says whether the whole answer is verified. G accounts also get an account block with spendable XLM; an unfunded or unknown G address answers 200 with `account: null` and no records. With as_of_ledger the holdings are read at a past ledger from the balance history (credit class assets-history, weight 5): include=closed is not available, unverified balances are not simulated, and publishable keys are not allowed. The history begins at read_view.bootstrap_ledger at the earliest; earlier ledgers need a snapshot job (`POST /snapshots`). Credit class assets-holdings: 1 × ceil(rows/100), at least one credit per started 64 KiB. Each unverified token simulated adds 1 credit. Publishable keys allowed.

- Unknown or repeated query parameters return 400, so a typo or an unsupported filter never returns unfiltered data.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Checksum-valid G or C address. An M… address resolves to its G account and the response carries muxed_input. B… and L… addresses are never holders.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only holdings of this kind.

parameters.name: min_balance
parameters.description: Decimal; holdings below it are left out.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma list: zero (zero-balance trustlines), closed (previously held, with closed_ledger), unverified (event-derived or simulated custom-token balances). Default: none of them.

parameters.name: asset
parameters.description: Only this asset: `native`, `CODE:ISSUER` (case-sensitive), a C… token contract ID or `pool:<64 hex>`. A Stellar Asset Contract ID matches the balances of its classic asset (CODE:ISSUER, or native for the native SAC), which records report under that classic ID.

parameters.name: as_of_ledger
parameters.description: Read at this past ledger from the balance history (credit class assets-history, weight 5). 400 when after the latest applied ledger; 409 when the history cannot answer it exactly. Not available to publishable keys.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Records per page, 1 to 200 (default 50).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Resume after this paging_token. Prefer following `_links.next.href`.

200.description: A page of holdings, the completeness block and, for a G account, the account entry.

completeness.note: every holding is read from protocol ledger entries or recognized SEP-41 storage

get.summary: List ranked holders of a token
get.description:
Holders ranked by balance descending, then holder ascending. For a classic asset this is one merged list of trustline and SAC contract holders. Zero balances only with include=zero. Deep pages are cursor-only. With as_of_ledger the holders are read at a past ledger from the balance history (credit class assets-history, weight 5); holder_count is the count at that ledger, and the `supply` key is present and null (supply_source does not apply); assets with more than 100,000 holders answer 409 and need a snapshot job. Credit class assets-holders: 5 × ceil(rows/100), at least one credit per started 64 KiB. Publishable keys are not allowed.

post.description: Starts a job that computes an address's holdings or an asset's holders at any past ledger from 63 on, including before bootstrap_ledger, from a history-archive checkpoint plus at most 63 replayed ledgers. Use it when an as_of_ledger read answers 409. The job runs in the background: poll `GET /snapshots/{id}` (the Location header). Holders results list at most the top 10,000 holders. An organization can have at most 5 jobs queued or running. Credit class assets-snapshot: 50 per job, charged on completion and released on failure. Publishable keys are not allowed.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional, 8 to 128 characters. Resending the same key with the same request returns the existing job (200, no new charge); the same key with a different request returns 409. It deduplicates on every plan, with no expiry.
